newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger in quiet session.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in quiet trade on Friday as yesterday's sharp drop in prices and short covering by traders strengthened the market, analysts said.

"There wasn't a huge amount of activity by any means today, but yesterday was a pretty big down day. There was some short covering," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Services.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.12 to C$112.92 to yield 6.924 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.64 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was 28 basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.
"It feels like the market is just in the habit of buying dips in Canada," said one Toronto-based bond trader. "It was pretty active in the morning but very light in the afternoon."

A report on the Canadian consumer price index for January had almost no impact on Canadian bonds, analysts said. The country's unadjusted January consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in the month and 2.2 percent in the year to 137.1, Statistics Canada said Friday. Economists had forecast the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.25 percent on the month.

Analysts said the next major event for the Canadian market will be the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday. The Canadian market will also be looking forward to the release of a report on Canada's currency account balance for the fourth quarter on Friday.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.18 to C$105.30 to yield 6.264 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.37 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to 11 basis points from 10 basis points on Thursday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.90 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.09 percent.
